name: Aaron Biliyok
currentRole: Lead Data Scientist at Helium Health
bio: Aaron Biliyok is a data scientist and engineer with over 8 years of experience building data-driven products across Africa's technology ecosystem, spanning automotive commerce, risk analytics, and healthcare. Aaron began his career at Andela, one of Africa's most selective talent accelerators, and evolved from software engineering into leading data science teams. He has held leadership roles at Cars45, Autochek Africa, and GoodLight, applying deep learning and statistical modeling to power commerce and risk assessment across emerging markets. Currently, as Lead Data Scientist at Helium Health, he leverages AI to improve healthcare delivery across the continent. Combining full-stack engineering depth with data science expertise, Aaron is passionate about using technology to unlock opportunities across Africa and committed to growing the next generation of technologists on the continent

name: Abdullahi Lawal
currentRole: Lead Treasury & Corporate Finance - Petrostuff Nigeria Ltd
bio: A finance professional and emerging investor, Abdullahi brings over 8 years of experience structuring capital, modelling transactions, and supporting growth across Nigeria's oilfield services sectors. Grounded in treasury, FP&A, and corporate finance, he has worked with TotalEnergies, Chevron, Shell, and Seplat Energy; with a growing conviction that financial rigour applied in upstream oil belongs in the hands of Africa's next generation of builders. Drawn to venture by a belief that capital allocation is one of the most powerful levers for structural change, he has a particular interest in energy transition, infrastructure, and financial inclusion. He is co-founder and CFO of LumoEV, a green energy startup, and is developing Waeed Altabie Ranch and Farms, a sustainable agriculture and aquaculture venture. Abdullahi is a Climate Leadership Fellow, holds an MSc in Accounting, and is an incoming Development Economics student at SOAS University of London. He is based in Lagos.

name: Adewale Oduye, JD, MBA
bio: Recognized by LinkedIn as a “Top Venture Capital Voice” in 2024, Adewale is a tech lawyer and advisor to early-stage startups with experience across sports, education, and healthcare. Most recently, he served as Director of Programs & Legal Affairs at Rhia Ventures, a social impact fund focused on maternal and reproductive health. There, he led legal operations and program strategy, advancing initiatives focused on inclusive due diligence, investor accountability, and impact-driven funding. Previously, Adewale served as Senior Counsel at the Los Angeles District Attorney’s Office, where he led white-collar criminal investigations involving multi-million-dollar fraud against large technology companies. Adewale also advises early-stage startups through Techstars and FoundersBoost. He earned his bachelor’s degree from Columbia University, law degree from Northwestern University, and MBA from the University of Southern California.

name: Alena Fesser
currentRole: Advisor for Investment & Trade Facilitation | Business Innovation
bio: Ambitious, curious and critical development professional working on sustainable economic growth with international experience across South America, Asia, and Africa. Strong track record in supporting startups and MSMEs across the venture lifecycle—from ideation and incubation to early-stage scaling—facilitating access to markets, partnerships, and financing. Experienced in engaging with founders, accelerators, and investors, as well as contributing to the design of catalytic capital solutions tailored to emerging market contexts. Focused on the intersection of entrepreneurship and capital allocation, with a particular interest in leveraging venture capital to address structural gaps in African ecosystems and enable scalable, impact-oriented businesses.

name: Aloaye Igiekhumhe
bio: Aloaye is a Nigerian legal practitioner with a decade of experience spanning compliance, corporate governance, and legal advisory. His career sits at the intersection of law, business, finance, and regulation, where he has helped founders and investors build resilient companies, structure products, and raise or deploy capital. He has advised on a wide range of transactions, including debt, equity, and hybrid fundraises, corporate and board reorganisations, market entry, and broader legal strategy. Beyond his professional work, Aloaye is committed to social impact. He leads the Give A Home A Book Project, a non‑profit dedicated to improving access to books by setting up libraries and donating reading materials to underserved communities, schools, and facilities in Nigeria. When he’s not working, Aloaye enjoys writing his newsletter, reading history and fiction, watching animation, and laughing loudly at a good comedy show.

name: Angelica Turner
bio: A seasoned Product and Program Management leader with over 20 years of experience, Angelica Turner drives strategic innovation at the intersection of data, technology, and customer experience. She currently leads high-impact initiatives at Amazon, where she has spent eight years delivering measurable results across global programs, optimizing operations, and advancing inclusive technology solutions. Originally from Austin, Texas, and now based in Atlanta, Georgia, she brings a unique blend of analytical rigor and people-centered leadership. Her cross-industry experience spans media, weather, mobile insurance, home improvement, and prepaid wireless, enabling her to translate complex challenges into actionable, scalable strategies. Known for connecting vision to execution, Angelica excels at building data-driven frameworks, aligning cross-functional teams, and delivering outcomes that influence both business performance and customer impact.

name: Ann Ichungwa
bio: Ms. CPA Ann Ichungwa is an investment and enterprise development specialist with over 10 years of experience accelerating early-stage enterprises across Africa at the intersection of entrepreneurship, venture building, and inclusive economic development. She is Managing Director of GAK Advisory Ltd, a Pan-African enterprise advisory firm enabling high-impact early-stage enterprises through market immersion, B2B facilitation, ecosystem partnerships, and tailored growth support. She is also Founder of Kap Capital, an angel investment fund backing early-stage African ventures with high growth and scalability potential. She has led investment readiness and due diligence work for donor-funded programs, DFIs, and private investors, including financial modeling, governance reviews, and market positioning for growth-stage enterprises. She has supported over 250 businesses to investment readiness, with many securing equity, debt, or blended finance. Through the Dream VC 2026 Fellowship, she seeks to deepen her venture capital expertise and strengthen her ability to support scalable enterprises across emerging markets.

name: Ann Ichungwa Ichungwa
bio: This was already submitted

name: Anna Ritz
currentRole: Strategy & Business Development at Visa, Venture Partner at Angel Invest Ventures
bio: Anna began her career almost two decades ago in development finance, focusing on public and private sector innovation, like green mobility financing, solar loans and social impact bonds, working across Tanzania, Kenya, India, Germany, and the UK with organizations including Ashoka, the German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs, the UK Cabinet Office, and the European Central Bank. Anna has since built a cross-sector career as operator, founder, and investor in financial infrastructure across Europe and Africa. She currently works at Visa, where she focuses on strategic business development in next-gen payment infrastructure. As Venture Partner and LP at Angel Invest, and Managing Director of Legata, she invests in startups that build the next generation of AI native financial tech stacks. Her vision is to contribute building a frictionless and instant global financial backbone for economies to scale beyond borders.

name: Arria Lakha
bio: Arria Lakha is an education leader passionate about driving innovation through experiential learning and student-led projects. With nearly a decade of experience working across Africa and globally, she has built and scaled educational programs that have impacted thousands of students. She also co-founded The Next Step Education, a consultancy delivering personalized education services to students across Kenya, Rwanda, and the DRC. At the African Leadership University, Arria worked closely with student entrepreneurs. Arria holds a BA in Ethnic Studies and Education Studies from Brown University. Arria is excited to explore venture capital, with an interest in investing in talent and early-stage startups across the continent.

name: Battista Baidoo
bio: Battista Baidoo is a Product Director with over ten years of experience building and scaling products at the intersection of AI, financial infrastructure, and payments. Currently based in London, she serves as a Product Director at Mastercard, where she leads the Financial Crime product portfolio for real-time payments across international markets. Prior to joining Mastercard, Battista was a Product Manager at ING Group in Amsterdam, where she led the delivery of the PSD2 APIs and supported the evolution of the trading finance platform. Her career has been defined by building complex, technically demanding products from zero to production, leading cross-functional teams spanning engineering, data science, operations, risk and commercial functions within some of the world’s leading financial institutions.

name: Bukonla Adebakin
bio: Bukonla Adebakin is a strategy, operations, and partnerships leader with over a decade of experience designing and executing systems that drive sustainable growth, institutional credibility, and measurable impact across Africa and emerging markets. Over the course of her career, she has mobilised more than $780,000 in cumulative funding through investment-ready concept development, high-stakes pitching, and the stewardship of complex stakeholder relationships. This capital has supported initiatives spanning governance, innovation, youth development, and policy-adjacent programmes with regional and international reach. In commercial and consulting environments, Bukonla has led strategy and execution efforts that diversified revenue streams, strengthened go-to-market models, and repositioned brands, delivering outcomes such as 45% quarter-on-quarter revenue growth and sustained improvements in operational performance. As the author of The Profit of Purpose and a facilitator of systems-thinking programmes, she brings both intellectual rigour and hands-on execution to every engagement.

name: Caroline Njuguna
bio: Caroline Njuguna is a venture builder and strategic operator passionate about driving social impact through innovation, entrepreneurship, and systems-level transformation across Africa. An MBA candidate and is also a certified PMP and CPA-K professional, with over 10 years of experience working across startups, venture building, and ecosystem development. Throughout her career, Caroline has worked with organizations including World Bank Group, GIZ, Uber, Mr. Green Africa, and Purple Elephant Ventures, supporting founders and ventures solving complex challenges across key sectors such as climate, supply chains and logistics, healthcare, tourism, technology, and inclusive economic development. Her work has contributed to scaling early-stage ventures, securing donor and ecosystem partnerships, , improving operational efficiency, unlocking funding, and managing high-impact initiatives driving sustainability and economic inclusion across the continent. Deeply inspired by the power of entrepreneurship to create meaningful change, Caroline is particularly interested in venture capital and venture support models that help founders build scalable, resilient, and high-impact companies. She is passionate about combining capital, strategy, and operational insight to build and support the next generation of transformative African businesses and the ecosystems that enable them to thrive.

name: Charles Fatunbi
bio: Charles Fatunbi is an Associate Manager at Accenture and creative entrepreneur focused on the technology and media sectors. With a background in Industrial & Systems Engineering and an MBA in Technology Innovation, he brings cross-functional experience in supply chain & operations, product development, and marketing. His clients have ranged from Fortune 100 companies and government agencies to nonprofits and early-stage startups. He founded Capsoul Creative, a boutique film production agency, and hosts Minds in Motion, a podcast highlighting underdog founders, creators, and industry experts driving impact at the intersection of technology, media, and culture. Charles is passionate about Africa's economic development and believes the continent's next generation of builders deserve the infrastructure and capital to fully realize it. He is pursuing DreamVC to grow as a future investor and operator while building his network across the African ecosystem. Outside of work, Charles is an avid traveler, fitness enthusiast, and loves to host!

name: Dagmawit Mengestu
location: Arlington/ Washington D.C. metro area, United States
bio: Dagmawit is an operator that started her career at Deloitte in talent acquisition, developing an early instinct for spotting potential that credentials alone don't capture. She then moved to IDEO.org and IDEO's Colab Venture Studio, working across financial inclusion, gender-lens investing, and digital access in Sub-Saharan Africa and Southeast Asia. She's currently a Research Fellow at Reframe Venture, equipping VCs with tools to integrate responsible investing in emerging markets. She arrives at Dream VC with an evolving thesis and the belief that lasting impact in the African venture ecosystem is built on inclusive market share, not charity. She holds a B.A. in International Affairs from UC Irvine and a Master of Public Policy from the University of Chicago, and is based in the Washington D.C. metro area. Community-building shows up everywhere in her life – from running the front desk at a local barre studio and learning the rhythms of a small business, to cooking, baking, and seeking out cultural events that keep her rooted.

name: Daniel Ogundare
bio: Daniel is a supply chain consultant with over ten years of experience building resilient healthcare and energy networks. His global career spans managing severe supply disruptions across Nigerian energy markets and securing Canada’s healthcare pipelines against volatile tariff pressures. With deep expertise in risk management and cross-border strategy, Daniel is passionate about leveraging venture capital to drive economic transformation across Africa. He partners with founders to build robust logistics infrastructure, prioritizing operational excellence and regional development. Outside of work, Daniel is a tennis and flag football player, currently pursuing the goal of completing all seven major world marathons.

name: Elizabeth Aro Aro
currentRole: Finance Specialist at Guaranty Trust Bank
bio: Elizabeth Aro is a First Class graduate of University of Ibadan, where she graduated as the best student in her department. She also earned a Distinction in Statistics during her National Diploma programme. She has over seven years of experience at Guaranty Trust Bank, rising to a senior finance and strategy specialist, with work-related exposure across Nigeria, India, and West Africa. Her experience spans credit risk management, financial modelling, investment analysis, valuation of investment securities, cross-border banking operations, offshore regulatory reporting, banking acquisition due diligence, and core banking transformation projects. Elizabeth is passionate about the role of capital in driving economic productivity, financial inclusion, and sustainable growth across Africa, particularly through supporting startups and SMEs. She holds certifications in PMP, FMVA, and currently at strategic professional level of the ACCA qualification. She will be joining the 2026 MBA cohort at London Business School as a LaidLaw Scholar.

name: Elyes Hachana
bio: Elyes Hachana is the founder of RISE, a boutique consultancy dedicated to design and build ventures to solve meaningful problems working alongside entrepreneurs, educators and policymakers across North Africa and the Western Mediterranean shores. He has over a decade of expertise in strategy and business development, youth empowerment, social innovation. Elyes Hachana previously served as Program Manager and Strategic Development Director within ENACTUS, an international nonprofit organization dedicated to inspiring students to improve the world through entrepreneurial action. He was also responsible for the entrepreneurship center within the Think & Do Tank IACE (Arab Institute Of Business Leaders). As a co-founder of Find Me he tackled the addressing system deficiency in Accra, Ghana. He also worked on the development of the first coworking space in Tunisia, Cogite Coworking Space, ranked by Forbes in the top ten coworking spaces on earth in 2016. Elyes holds a Master’s Degree in Business Intelligence and a Bachelor’s in Management from the prestigious IHEC Carthage.

name: Emma Garcia Ligero
bio: Emma Garcia-Ligero is an investment professional with a background spanning private equity, venture capital, and impact investing. She began her career in PE at Eurazeo, then moved into HealthTech growth equity at Lauxera Capital Partners, and early-stage VC at Newfund Capital, backing European founders scaling into the US across multiple verticals. At Shift4Good, she honed her impact investment skills across climate and industry. Emma holds a Master in Management from ESCP Business School, with a dual major in Finance and Entrepreneurship. Her connection to Africa is personal and deep: she grew up in Madagascar, learned Swahili at INALCO, and walked 7,000km solo from Paris to Dakar in 2024. Today, her focus sits at the intersection of early-stage devtools, mass-market impact, and AI built in Africa for global markets. She is building an initiative to bridge European corporates and African startups.

name: Emma Ruiters
currentRole: Manager at Tony Blair Institute for Global Change
bio: Emma Ruiters is a Manager at the Tony Blair Institute for Global Change (TBI), advising governments on digital economy, innovation ecosystems, and industrial policy. Emma founded and led a South African EdTech business from 2020 until its successful exit. She has worked with organisations including Meta, the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, and the Omidyar Network. Emma's work has been published by the Tony Blair Institute for Global Change, UK in a Changing Europe, Daily Maverick, Business Day, The Africa Report, Genesis Analytics, and forthcoming in the Routledge Handbook of Asian Powers in Africa. Her commentary has also been featured by African Business and King's College London. She previously served as Policy Lead for the Labour Africa Network. A South African based in London who also speaks Japanese, Emma holds master's degrees from the University of Oxford and SOAS University of London.

name: Esmat Osama
bio: Esmat Osama is a startup ecosystem and partnerships professional with 7+ years of experience across Egypt and the Gulf, working with accelerators, VCs, UN initiatives, and entrepreneurship programs. She has led and supported startup growth, strategic partnerships, and innovation programs with organizations including Flat6Labs, E3 Ventures, Tech Horizons Ventures, and UN organizations. Passionate about entrepreneurship and impact-driven innovation, Esmat is dedicated to building meaningful collaborations that empower founders and strengthen regional ecosystems.

name: Eya Chemli
currentRole: Head of Partnerships at Open Startup
bio: Eya is an entrepreneurship and innovation professional with over 10 years of experience supporting startups, SMEs, and innovation ecosystems across Africa. She currently serves as Head of Partnerships at Open Startup, a pan-African acceleration organization supporting pre-seed and seed-stage startups, where she leads strategic partnerships, fundraising, and sustainability efforts to support entrepreneurs and strengthen innovation ecosystems across the continent. Previously, she worked as a Senior Manager at Deloitte Africa, advising African governments, multilateral donors, and corporates on innovation strategy, entrepreneurship development, feasibility studies, and ecosystem-building initiatives. She led and implemented projects aimed at supporting startups, SMEs, and inclusive economic growth across the region. Earlier in her career, Eya contributed to USAID-funded projects in Tunisia and the United States focused on economic empowerment, private sector development, and entrepreneurship support. She holds a Bachelor’s degree in Finance and a professional certificate in Entrepreneurship from the Kelley School of Business. Eya is passionate about innovation, impact-driven entrepreneurship, and animal welfare.

name: Farah Mami
bio: Farah Mami is an investor and operator whose 14-year career has never fit a single box — and that is precisely her edge. Across law, finance, and business building, she has moved fluidly between disciplines, stepping into a complex family investment context and transforming how it operates: building governance frameworks from scratch, assembling the right people around the table, and expanding its scope across multiple jurisdictions spanning North Africa, the UK, and the Gulf. Her most formative work has been in high-stakes, ambiguous environments — originating UK greenfield investments with no playbook, mitigating multi-jurisdictional risk, and closing tough negotiations that required equal parts legal rigour, financial acuity, and human intelligence. Her formal training in law (LLM) and finance (BCom) underpins it all, alongside a long-standing intellectual engagement with philosophy, systems thinking, and human behaviour. As former Chair of YPO Tunisia and an officer on multiple international boards spanning business, trade, and women's leadership, Farah has operated at the highest levels of peer leadership across continents. At Dream VC, she is channelling this cross-disciplinary depth into the African venture ecosystem — as a builder, an investor, and a connector of capital to conscious leadership.

name: Firas Rhaiem
bio: mention working in M&A, BIotechs, Counsulting A Tunisian entrepreneur and founder of Clarrio, a healthtech data aggregation platform focused on transforming fragmented healthcare information into actionable intelligence. With an engineering background and an international upbringing across the GCC and North America, he brings a global perspective to building scalable technology solutions at the intersection of healthcare, data, and innovation. His professional experience spans mergers & acquisitions, Life science, and consulting, where he developed expertise in strategic growth, market analysis, and operational transformation. Combining technical depth with business acumen, he has worked across multidisciplinary environments ranging from fast-paced startups to complex corporate ecosystems.

name: Florence Adu
currentRole: CEO, LEAP Transmedia Productions + Managing Director, ArgoAdu LLC
bio: Florence Amerley Adu is social entrepreneur and project management consultant based in Accra, Ghana and Brooklyn, New York. As founder and CEO of LEAP Transmedia Productions, a content development and production company based in Accra, Florence is invested in nurturing future minds through foundational learning, thought provoking audiovisual experiences and accessible technologies. LEAP, an acronym for Learning, Education, Arts and People, is an expression of her passion for improving education and economic outcomes for Ghanaians and Africans across the Diaspora. Aside from writing and producing edutaining content for children and parenting resources for adults, Florence is the host of the Glocal Citizens podcast, which, through thoughtful discussions with dynamic Diasporans, aims to inspire a borderless mindset around manifesting a new world with a particularly Pan-African perspective. Florence is also Managing Director of ArgoAdu LLC, a project management company. The ArgoAdu portfolio includes real estate, construction and property management projects in Denver, New York and Accra. Florence spent a significant part of her more than 25-year career focusing on community/economic development and merging her interest in improving the built environment with her technical background in engineering and public policy. A vocal advocate for work-life balance, Florence always makes time for travel, especially unique adventures while exploring other cultures. She is an avid runner, yogi and lifestylist.

name: Florent Parmentier
bio: Florent Parmentier (French & Canadian) A former Humanitarian/International Development field Operator and multi-sector Professional, Florent started his career in the Aerospace Industry and has over 20 years of experience in funding acquisition, strategy advisory, leadership and partnership development across France, Canada,The Caribbean and Africa. Passionate about innovation and tech enthusiast, Florent recently started his journey into VC, driven by the connections he made, throughout his time in the Caribbean and Africa, with young talents and entrepreneurs eager to develop and scale their disruptive and innovative products and services. Most recently, Florent joined the Venture in residence Program of LvlUp Ventures while continuing his work as an Advisor in the Insurance industry.

name: Ham Namakajjo
currentRole: Country Manager, Uganda at Ankolo Consulting
bio: Ham Namakajjo is a Uganda-based strategy executive, business coach, and entrepreneur with a career spanning management consulting, global technology, and venture building. He honed his analytical foundations at Bain & Company in Los Angeles before leading market development at Google Uganda, scaling Jumia Uganda, and driving collective action to solve entrepreneurial ecosystem challenges at the Uganda Entrepreneurial Ecosystem Initiative. Today, as Country Manager at Ankolo Consulting, he helps SMEs access financing by making them investment-ready through strategic positioning and supporting them through strategy development and change management. Alongside this, he is Venture Lead for Project Silicon, an initiative to establish Uganda's first metallurgical-grade silicon manufacturing industry, developed in collaboration with the Science, Technology & Innovation Secretariat in the Office of the President. He also serves on the board of XENO Investment, a Ugandan fintech democratizing access to wealth management. Ham holds an MBA from The Wharton School.

name: Hamza Elessawy
bio: Hamza Elessawy (Egyptian) has spent seven years with great teams at the seam between sectors he didn't start out in, credit infrastructure, computer vision, healthcare AI. He was the first Technical PM at I-SCORE, Egypt's national credit bureau. At Tapway in Malaysia, he led product through a turnaround during which the team launched the country's first computer vision ISV on AWS Marketplace. He co-founded Pixelence with a clinical oncologist and a business leader, a medical imaging AI eliminating gadolinium contrast in brain MRI, now in clinical trials and EIC Phase 1 approved. He earlier co-founded Skip Pay across Egypt, Libya, and Iraq; people he built with have gone on to lead across MENA's regional finance and sovereign institutions. He co-directs AI Tinkerers Malaysia, and is finishing the Erasmus Mundus Master in Impact Entrepreneurship (EMMIE). At Dream VC he is learning, alongside this cohort, how to back operators building in MENA, Africa, and SEA.

name: Idongesit Inyang
currentRole: Client Success Executive at Solt Advisory, LLC
bio: Idongesit Inyang is a customer experience and operations professional with over 10 years of experience spanning banking, advisory, customer experience, and service management. He has built strong expertise in customer engagement, complaint management, process optimization, employee experience, and service delivery transformation through roles at organizations including United Bank for Africa, Sterling Bank, and Solt Advisory. A lifelong learner, he is passionate about reading, research, and continuous personal development. Outside work, he is a Tupac Shakur fan and enjoys building meaningful, long-lasting relationships.

name: IFEOLUWA MARTINS
currentRole: Access to Learning and Work Tools Manager at CcHUB
bio: Ifeoluwa Martins is an innovation and ecosystem strategist working at the intersection of innovation, access, and economic opportunity. His work focuses on designing and delivering programs that enable individuals, SMEs, and tech startups to grow within evolving digital economies across Africa. Currently, he serves as Access to Learning & Work Tools Manager at CcHUB, where he leads large scale initiatives expanding access to workspaces, connectivity, and digital tools for thousands of participants across Nigeria. Previously, he led Lagos Innovates at the Lagos State Employment Trust Fund (LSETF), collaborating across government, private sector, and development ecosystems to support startup growth, digital talent development, and SME resilience. Across his career, he has supported over 1,000 startups and 5,000 SMEs through programs spanning access to finance, infrastructure, mentorship, and capacity building. His interests lie in inclusive digital economies, venture capital, AI governance, and building scalable systems that expand access to work, learning, and opportunity across Africa.

name: Ikenna Okekeogbu
currentRole: Research Scientist at Charles River Laboratories
bio: Ikenna Okekeogbu is a life sciences professional with a PhD in Biological Engineering whose career spans academic research, translational science, and drug development. He has worked across academia, a postdoctoral fellowship at Pfizer focused on building platforms to enhance drug safety research, and in the CRO industry, where he supports bioanalytical studies for drug candidates advancing toward regulatory review. Through these experiences, he has developed a strong interest in how scientific discovery translates into real-world therapeutic and commercial impact. Alongside his scientific work, Ikenna has explored the business and investment side of life sciences through hands-on healthtech startup due diligence and investment assessment. Originally from Nigeria, he is particularly drawn to the long-term potential of Africa’s healthcare and biotechnology ecosystem and is interested in how science, innovation, and capital can work together to strengthen health systems and support meaningful progress across the continent.

name: Janeth Kateya
bio: Janeth Kateya is a dynamic professional with a diverse career spanning banking, mobile financial services, asset financing, entrepreneurship and enterprise development. A social impact intrapreneur Janeth possesses versatile skills chief among them relationship management which enable her to drive impact. Her current work with PUM – a Dutch based NGO involves facilitating training and capacity building for Zimbabwean entrepreneurs by PUM experts. Her efforts have culminated in collaboration within the tourism and hospitality industry. The sum total of her experiences has imbued her with invaluable strategic insights into the challenges faced by African startups as well as a sense of duty to promote transformational financing in Africa, Janeth is dedicated to making a global impact.

name: Jola J. Atoki
bio: An operator and strategic advisor, Jola supports ambitious businesses in going from 0 to 1 through creative partnerships, talent strategy, go-to-market execution, and investor readiness preparation. Inspired by the potential of the venture and innovation ecosystem to drive rapid economic growth and a conviction to consistently deliver value with excellence, she is particularly interested in deploying capital into education, consumer brands, technology, cultural exchange, and cross-border businesses across the Africa-Asia corridor. With a background in law and business, Jola has worked across EdTech, intellectual property protection, beauty and wellness, and innovation ecosystems, where she has led partnerships, GTM execution, operational transformation, and growth strategy in emerging market contexts. Known for her ability to identify under-explored trends early, she is passionate about connecting ideas, industries, and people to unlock scalable opportunities across local and global markets.

name: Joy Enechukwu
currentRole: Senior Operations Manager at Endeavor Nigeria
bio: Joy Enechukwu is a Lagos-based operations and ecosystem professional working at Endeavor Nigeria, where she supports high-impact entrepreneurs and founders building scalable businesses across Africa. Her work focuses on operational strategy, program execution, and ecosystem coordination within the startup and entrepreneurship landscape. With a growing interest in venture capital and founder enablement, Joy is particularly interested in how investment and operational support can help unlock sustainable growth across emerging markets. Through the Dream VC Investor Accelerator, she aims to deepen her understanding of the African investment ecosystem and contribute to the next generation of transformative startups on the continent. Outside of work, Joy is a marathon runner.

name: Joy Kathure Mutunga
bio: Joy is an investment and ecosystem professional whose experience spans venture building, financial services, and early-stage innovation ecosystems across Africa. She has built experience across venture building at Pyramidia Venture Studio and financial services at CIC Group, supporting initiatives related to market research, analysis, due diligence, and business evaluation. Her work has included exposure to climate-focused ventures, emerging market innovation, and investment-oriented analytical projects. Joy holds a background in Economics and is particularly interested in the intersection of finance, technology, and impact across emerging markets. She is passionate about venture investing, ecosystem development, and expanding access to capital and innovation within Africa’s entrepreneurial landscape.

name: Katharina Weber
currentRole: Senior Project Leader at Open Capital
bio: Katharina Weber is a strategy and investment professional working at the intersection of impact investing, blended finance, and ecosystem development across African markets. She currently works in management consulting, supporting investors, DFIs, foundations, and high-growth businesses on investment strategy, pipeline development, market assessments, investment readiness, and innovative financing approaches across sectors including agriculture, climate, energy access, and gender. Over the past years, she has worked across key parts of the investment lifecycle, including pipeline building, due diligence, fundraising, and portfolio support, contributing to the development and screening of pipelines covering more than 1,300 companies and supporting nearly USD 60 million across investment vehicles, financing facilities, companies, and market-building initiatives across Africa. Alongside her consulting work, Katharina is also active as an angel investor and mentor supporting early-stage founders across the continent.

name: Kelvin Nzau
currentRole: Global Business Transformation Leader at Sun King
bio: Kelvin is the Global Business Transformation leader at Sun King, where he leads cross-functional work across new market expansions, service innovations, and large-scale change initiatives. As such, his experience spans go-to-market execution, process innovation, operational excellence, and scaling explorative initiatives across multiple African markets. Before Sun King, Kelvin held scaling roles at One Acre Fund and Little, building experience across operations, growth, and process improvement in fast-moving environments. Having spent close to nine years at companies actively building and scaling, he brings an operator’s perspective to questions of growth, viability, and scale. He is interested in the climate space, particularly renewable energy, and in the gap between operator insights and investment decision-making in Africa. His goal is to build stronger bridges between the realities of operators on the ground and how capital is deployed across Africa. Kelvin holds an MBA from Strathmore Business School (SBS) and is a YALI alumn.

name: Magalie Laliberte
bio: Magalie Laliberté has over 10 years of experience in the impact sector across West Africa — Benin, Ghana, Mali, Senegal, and Togo — as an international development worker and grant professional. Her work focuses on entrepreneurship and youth development, and CSO capacity strengthening. She has coordinated youth-inclusion programs, designed entrepreneurship training curricula, and secured more than $2 million in public and private funding for programs serving young people and African entrepreneurs. She holds an Executive MBA from Quantic School of Business & Technology and a graduate degree in Communication. She is a fellow at the New England Impact Investing Initiative (NEIII), where she has deepened her expertise in social finance. Born in Haiti and raised in Canada, she is fluent in French and English. Magalie has long been interested in the African continent’s development and the return of its diaspora. She is currently based between Montreal, Canada, and Cotonou, Benin.

name: Marcel Schlobach
bio: Marcel is a startup ecosystem builder passionate about supporting founders tackling the climate crisis. He most recently spent over seven years as a Principal at the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) in London, where he co-led the Star Venture programme and supported the growth of early-stage startups across 25+ emerging markets through tailored advisory, access to capital, and a global network of mentors and corporates. Earlier in his career, he structured blended finance solutions to mobilise climate investment, and gained further experience in consulting, think tanks, government and the UN. As a Mercator Fellow on International Affairs, Marcel is now based in Nairobi, joining Persistent, a climate tech VC fund and venture builder, to deepen his exposure to early-stage investing on the continent. He holds an M.Sc. in International Economic Policy from Sciences Po Paris and has lived, studied and worked in ten countries across three continents.

name: Mawusee Foli-Awli
currentRole: Director at Hit Higher Consulting Inc.
bio: Mawusee Foli-Awli is a multidisciplinary professional, entrepreneur, and ecosystem builder with over 20 years of experience spanning technology, project management, business development, and finance. Having worked across Africa and Canada, he has collaborated with startups, entrepreneurs, and community-driven initiatives to support innovation, strategic growth, and knowledge sharing. He began his career as a software developer before moving into leadership and advisory roles, managing complex projects and helping organizations deliver measurable impact. Passionate about entrepreneurship and emerging ecosystems, Mawusee is particularly interested in bridging opportunities between Africa and global markets through innovation, education, and investment. Known for his collaborative and multicultural approach, he combines technical expertise, strategic thinking, and strong communication skills to help founders and communities grow sustainably.

name: MICHAEL KAMAU
currentRole: ASSISTANT FINANCE MANAGER - CIC ASSET MANAGERS
bio: Michael Kamau is a finance and investment professional with experience in pension administration, fund accounting, and financial asset management within Kenya’s financial services sector. He currently works in finance at CIC Asset Managers Kenya, supporting financial reporting, treasury operations, governance processes, and investment-related activities. Passionate about sustainable growth and efficient capital allocation across African markets, Michael has a strong interest in asset management, corporate governance and strategic finance. His experience spans pension funds, unit trusts, and alternative investments, with exposure to regulatory compliance, budgeting, and portfolio administration. Michael is also pursuing academic research focused on executive compensation, board gender diversity, and firm performance among firms listed on the Nairobi Securities Exchange. Beyond work, he enjoys watching and playing football and engaging in discussions on business and investment trends.

name: mohamed ali aboudi
bio: Mohamed Ali ABOUDI Associate & Partner – MAAP Mohamed Ali ABOUDI is a communication strategist, business development expert, and innovation advisor with extensive experience across the Maghreb, MENA region, and Africa. He has developed and led strategic communication, business development, and partnership initiatives for international organizations, institutions, and private sector brands. He is recognized for his expertise in communication management and stakeholder engagement, notably as an expert in communication and complaints management for the World Bank-funded project Innovative SMEs & Startups in Tunisia. Deeply involved in innovation ecosystems across Africa, Mohamed Ali ABOUDI actively supports entrepreneurship, foresight, and strategic transformation initiatives. He also serves as a strategy advisor and contributed to launching InnovAfricaDeals, a dedicated innovation and business section developed in partnership with African Business, promoting innovation-driven opportunities and collaboration across the continent. Mohamed Ali ABOUDI graduated from the Ecole Supérieure de Commerce de Tunis in International Business and holds a Master’s degree in Entrepreneurship and Business Development. He has completed several executive trainings in foresight strategy, innovation management, and international marketing, and is currently pursuing an MBA. His career includes leadership positions with Groupe Jeune Afrique, where he managed executive development and support missions in Africa for over 10 years, as well as serving for nearly 8 years as Regional Exam Manager MENA North and consultant for the British Council.

name: Nate Cheruiyot
currentRole: Senior Investment Associate at DOB Equity
bio: Nathan (Nate) Cheruiyot is a Senior Investment Associate at DOB Equity, a Dutch family office-backed investment fund deploying patient capital into Seed to Series A businesses across East Africa. He focuses on the fund's sustainable food systems, renewable energy, and water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) verticals, supporting founders building enterprises that combine commercial discipline with impact at scale. Prior to DOB, Nate was with Goodwell Investments, where he executed venture debt transactions across East Africa in sectors including sustainable agriculture, renewable energy, and clean mobility. He began his career at Open Capital Advisors, working closely with small and growing businesses across Sub-Saharan Africa on financing, operations, and growth strategy. Nate holds a Bachelor of Economics and Statistics from the University of Nairobi. He is passionate about the role of founder-aligned capital in unlocking inclusive growth across East Africa's most underserved sectors. Outside of work, he enjoys a good weekend run.

name: Nebiyou Yirga
currentRole: General Manager of Ethiopian Association of Startup Ecosystem
bio: Nebiyou is a startup ecosystem builder and entrepreneurship program leader with over 10 years of experience designing and delivering founder-facing programs across Ethiopia's emerging tech landscape. He currently serves as General Manager of the Ethiopian Association of Startup Ecosystems (EASE), where he leads structured programs spanning public-private dialogue and ecosystem development — contributing directly to the drafting and enactment of the Ethiopian Startup Act. As an entrepreneurship consultant for Gebeya Inc. under IFC and MasterCard Foundation mandates, he coached 200+ startups across cohorts of 40–50 founders, supporting them from customer discovery through product-market fit. Earlier, as founder of Splash Interactive, he scaled an Amharic-language mobile application to 1.5 million organic users with zero paid distribution — demonstrating rare product intuition for underserved, non-English-speaking markets. Nebiyou holds a GMBA in Startup, Innovation & Entrepreneurship from Tel Aviv University and a BSc in Computer Science from RMIT.

name: Nyunyuzi Dennis
bio: Dennis Nyunyuzi Brollins is a seasoned operator and ecosystem builder with over 11 years of experience scaling businesses across East Africa. As Managing Director of GreenBay Market Kenya, he built East Africa's first certified circular economy recommerce marketplace, securing $450K from CLASP, IKEA Foundation, and Carbon Trust. Previously, Dennis built MarketForce Uganda to $21M in revenue with 60 employees and scaled Wasoko Uganda's monthly GMV from $100K to $2.6M. His experience spans both B2B and B2C models across Uganda, Kenya, Rwanda, and Tanzania. Dennis has also served as an Investment Associate at Century Oak Ventures in Tanzania, where he gained early exposure to capital deployment and deal structuring. Passionate about the intersection of commerce, technology, and sustainability, Dennis aims to transition from operator to investor, leveraging his deep market knowledge and operational expertise to back the next generation of African founders building scalable, impactful businesses.

name: Olivier Tameze-Rivas
bio: Olivier is an investment professional with a background in M&A and venture capital. Born in Cameroon with roots in Equatorial Guinea, he began his career as an investment banker at Citi in London, advising on digital infrastructure transactions. Most recently, he worked as a consultant on ChatGPT for Excel, contributing to OpenAI's effort to bring AI capabilities into enterprise financial workflows. A former D1 athlete with an MBA from Cornell University, he is passionate about early-stage investing across sports, health, and wellness. He serves on the board of Marathon Kids, a national nonprofit using technology to track movement and build healthy habits in kids. He is based in Venice, CA.

name: Oluwadamilola Akinloye
currentRole: Head of Programs, Venture Platform Funds
bio: Damilola is a Program Manager with nearly a decade of experience designing and managing high-impact entrepreneurship and ecosystem development programs across Africa. Her work has largely focused on supporting early-stage and women-led businesses through accelerators, partnerships, investment readiness initiatives, and capacity-building programs. She currently works at Ventures Platform, where she contributes to initiatives focused on diversifying venture capital and strengthening access for underrepresented founders across the continent. Over the years, she has worked across development, innovation, and startup ecosystems, managing multi-stakeholder partnerships and programs that connect founders to capital, mentorship, and growth opportunities. Outside of work, Damilola is passionate about storytelling, entrepreneurship, and community building. She has a background in cinematography and enjoys exploring how narrative can shape culture, opportunity, and impact across Africa.

name: Omatsola Otubu
bio: Omatsola is an investment professional with eight years of experience developing, structuring and financing bankable infrastructure projects across East, Central and West Africa, spanning power, natural resources, heavy industry and transport. Beyond infrastructure, he has an interest in early-stage African businesses and the role venture capital and angel investing play in financing them. This has driven him to deepen his understanding of early stage investing and expand his perspective across the African venture capital landscape.

name: OMOLE IMOSEMI
bio: Omole Imosemi is a senior professional with a keen interest in work at the nexus of impact and innovative finance towards delivering strong financial returns alongside sustainable positive outcomes. Her recent experience includes roles within the Impact Economy team at the UK Government’s Civil Society and Youth Directorate and NatWest Social & Community Capital, with exposure across social investment and outcomes-based funding. Prior to this, she founded BrandLee Solutions, a social enterprise through which she launched the innovative “Bookbased Learning” methodology a B2B capacity-building service delivered across 40+ organisations, alongside youth-focused community initiatives aimed at fostering lifelong learning. Her 16-year career spans banking, telecommunications, retail, consulting, and brand leadership, including managing marketing strategy for Nigeria’s foremost premium paint brands. Omole holds an MSc in Social Innovation and Entrepreneurship from the London School of Economics and Political Science (LSE), where she was a Standard Bank Africa Chairman Scholar. She also holds an MBA, a Bachelor's degree in Economics and Statistics, and is an On Purpose Fellow.

name: Princess Oti
currentRole: Group Chief Operating Officer and Head of Legal at PAM Africa
bio: Princess Oti (Nigerian) Princess Oti is a lawyer, operator, and venture builder working at the intersection of energy, finance, and technology in Africa. She began her career in corporate and commercial law before co-founding a cross-border fintech venture recognised by TechCrunch, the Royal Academy of Engineering, Inclusive Fintech 50, building it from infancy through to institutional partnerships. Today, she serves as Group Chief Operating Officer of PAM Africa, an Energy Enabler Ecosystem delivering clean energy infrastructure, EPC and O&M services, and AI-driven energy intelligence across the continent. In this role, she leads multi-million-dollar project execution, structures financing arrangements, and negotiates strategic agreements with DFIs, utilities, and governments. Beyond her operational work, she mentors early-stage founders and young people navigating the African business, technology and career landscape. Recognised by Innovate Finance as a 2023 Women in Fintech Powerlist Senior Industry Leader, Princess joins the Dream VC 2026 cohort to move from enabling high-impact businesses to actively backing and scaling them.

name: Rahma Hammami
bio: Rahma Hammami is a pan-African growth operator with seven years of experience scaling organisations across Africa and the Middle East. At GoMyCode, she opened seven country offices across Tunisia, Morocco, Egypt, Algeria, Nigeria, Côte d'Ivoire, and Senegal, growing student intake from 4,000 to over 10,000, before leading market entry in Abu Dhabi from the ground up. Holding a Finance degree from IHEC, Rahma has built her career at the intersection of institutional partnerships and market expansion, working alongside development partners including Expertise France and PNUD. She joins Dream VC's Investor Accelerator to translate seven years of pan-African operator experience into investment perspective, and to contribute to how capital shapes Africa's growing startup ecosystem.

name: Ramasamy Venugopal
currentRole: Operations Manager, International Astronomical Union's Office of Astronomy for Development
bio: Ramasamy works at the intersection of space/astronomy, impact, and capital. Currently managing grant portfolios and programmes that support astronomy and space projects across 100+ countries, he works with universities and research institutions to strengthen the application of science towards sustainable development. His work spans designing programs and funding mechanisms, managing portfolios, and building communities around science-driven initiatives that turn technical ideas into measurable, scalable outcomes. Previously, he trained as an electronics and communications engineer and worked in the telecommunications industry, before completing his Master's in Space Studies at the International Space University. That technical foundation, combined with years spent working alongside researchers, founders, and funders, gives him a systems-level view of how innovation moves from concept to real-world impact. Ram is positioning himself at the frontier of space and astronomy venture investing, to back technical founders building the next generation of space ventures in Africa and emerging markets.

name: Robert Kimbui
bio: Dr. Robert Kimbui is a global health and pharmaceutical supply chain leader with over 15 years of experience across Africa, Europe, and emerging markets. He currently serves as Project Lead for the SECURE initiative at the Global Antibiotic Research and Development Partnership (GARDP), where he works with international partners to improve sustainable access to essential antibiotics. With a background spanning pharmacy, health economics, and end-to-end supply chain strategy, Robert has led initiatives in Integrated business planning, market shaping and access planning for critical medicines. Prior to joining GARDP, he held regional leadership roles at Johnson & Johnson, supporting pharmaceutical supply chain transformation and access programs across EMEA. Robert is passionate about the intersection of global health, innovation, and investment, with a growing focus on how venture capital and strategic financing can accelerate scalable healthcare solutions in emerging markets.

name: Rodney Carew
currentRole: Head of Portfolio Performance at FSD Africa Investments
bio: Rodney Carew is Head of Portfolio Performance at FSD Africa Investments. He brings over a decade of experience building and scaling impact-focused initiatives across Africa. He has worked with investors, development organisations, and early-stage ventures to design financing mechanisms, mobilise capital, and support companies advancing climate and economic resilience. Before FSDAi, he was Chief of Staff and Head of Investor Relations at Delta40 Venture Studio, leading capital raising, investor engagement, and firm strategy while supporting climate tech ventures. He also held leadership roles at BESTSELLER Foundation, Factor[e] Ventures, and Equator Africa, where he led post-investment support for over 30 climate tech ventures, built portfolio management systems, and drove value creation partnerships. Earlier, Rodney spent eight years at Open Capital Advisors, launching and leading the Southern Africa office and working across sectors including agriculture, renewable energy, financial services, and healthcare. He began his career at Wipro advising Fortune 500 firms on restructuring and IT strategy. Rodney holds an MSc in Management from Wake Forest University and a BA from Northwestern University.

name: Shantelle Awomoyi
bio: Shantelle Awomoyi is an experienced frontier technology professional operating across venture, product, and ecosystem building. She holds a First Class Master’s degree in Materials Science and Engineering from the University of Manchester, where she graduated first in her cohort with the highest examination marks. She began her career in nuclear energy and B2B fintech before moving into blockchain infrastructure, working with leading organisations including Gnosis and Golem, where she is currently Head of Ecosystem. Her work spans product go-to-market, strategic partnerships, founder support, and ecosystem development. She has worked across the platform and investment strategy functions of two funds totalling $100M and helped deploy capital into African and global developer ecosystems. An alumna of Entrepreneurs First and recognised for her award-winning ecosystem initiatives, Shantelle advocates for greater access to frontier technology careers and is focused on backing scalable companies that turn Africa’s structural gaps into globally relevant opportunities.

name: Sipho Dikweni
bio: Sipho is a Commercialisation Manager at the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR), where he focuses on capital allocation and investment into IP-driven ventures with the objective of scaling innovation into investable, exit-ready businesses. His work sits at the intersection of venture investment, technology commercialisation, and portfolio development, with a strong focus on identifying opportunities where technology, market demand, and capital efficiency intersect to unlock scalable growth. Over the past decade, Sipho has worked extensively with universities, research institutions, and SMMEs to evaluate intellectual property, assess underlying technologies, structure ventures, and support their progression from early-stage innovation to commercially viable businesses. His experience spans deal sourcing, investment structuring, portfolio management, IP due diligence, technology transfer, and commercial strategy. Sipho has developed a strong lens for assessing investability, with particular interest in bridging the gap between innovation and capital by deploying the right investment structures, strategic direction, and partnerships to unlock long-term commercial value and sustainable exits.

name: Solomon Ngoma
currentRole: Enterprise Development Specialist at National Technology Business Centre (NTBC)
bio: Solomon Ngoma is an Enterprise Development Specialist at the National Technology Business Centre, where he supports startups and innovators through business incubation, commercialization, market linkages, and enterprise development programs. He also manages innovation financing initiatives, including startup funding and business support programs aimed at helping high-potential ventures scale sustainably. Solomon plays an active role in strengthening Zambia’s entrepreneurial ecosystem through startup acceleration, ecosystem partnerships, and innovation support initiatives, with a strong passion for helping entrepreneurs transform ideas into viable businesses.

name: Soraya Hosni
bio: Soraya Hosni is a French-Tunisian social entrepreneur, Yale World Fellow, and advisor to impact investors and family offices. Through her own ventures, she is reviving the craft and architecture of historic Islamic cities and building the technology layer that brings sustainability, traceability, and fair pricing to global agricultural supply chains. Her conviction is : the world's most overlooked communities are sitting on its most valuable assets and the next generation of returns will come from backing them. She advises the investors ready to move first.

name: Stephanie Ugo
currentRole: Manager, Content Advisement at Walt Disney Studios
bio: Stephanie Ugo is a producer, creative strategist, and entertainment specialist with experience spanning production, development, and content strategy across leading media and entertainment companies. Currently at Disney Studios, where she manages content strategy and advisement across Marvel, 20th Century, and Searchlight Pictures, her background includes overseeing film, television, and multimedia projects from development through distribution across major franchises and brands, with previous experience at DreamWorks Animation. Across her career, Stephanie has developed a sharp instinct for identifying commercially viable ideas and shaping them for global audiences, merging storytelling, development, creative strategy, and brand positioning to move projects from concept to impact. Her expertise spans the creative pipeline, giving her a unique perspective on the creative, strategic, and commercial forces shaping the entertainment industry. Passionate about the future of Africa's creative economy, Stephanie is focused on expanding how African and diaspora stories are developed, positioned, and experienced globally while helping strengthen long-term infrastructure and build creative equity across the continent's entertainment ecosystem.

name: Steve Mwangangi
currentRole: Pipeline Management Lead at Seven Capital Ventures
bio: Steve Mwangangi is an investment professional, angel investor, and corporate lawyer focused on backing technologies that transform lives and economies. He leads pipeline management at Seven Capital Ventures, an early-stage VC fund investing globally across fintech, artificial intelligence, logistics, and e-commerce. Steve began his investment journey at Future Africa, a pioneering fund backing visionary African founders, before building legal expertise at Bowmans, Africa’s premier commercial law firm. Beyond venture capital, he is an avid boxer, hiker, and youth mentor. He coordinates mentorship for university students worldwide through paNhari and the Talloires Network of Engaged Universities, and is also the co-founder of a hiking company in Kenya that uses outdoor experiences to drive environmental conservation, community outreach, and youth development.

name: Steve Tchoumba
bio: Steve Tchoumba is a pan‑African innovation ecosystem executive and AfriLabs Board Secretary with 10+ years leading institutions across digital innovation, entrepreneurship, and early‑stage finance. As Executive Manager of ActivSpaces, he has delivered multi‑donor programs (AFD, GIZ, World Bank, OIF) supporting founders and hubs, and led cross‑sector coalitions such as the 237 Digital Trade Innovation Lab to operationalize AfCFTA opportunities. His experience spans policy advocacy, partnerships, fundraising, financial oversight, operations and team leadership, and international representation.

name: Yomna El-Awamri
currentRole: CEO at Yimpakt / Egypt Country Manager at PUM Netherlands
bio: Yomna El-Awamri is the founder and CEO of Yimpakt, a Cairo-based impact venture, and serves as Egypt Country Manager for PUM Netherlands, where she connects Egyptian SMEs with international expertise to strengthen competitiveness and unlock growth. With over a decade of experience across climate, investment readiness, and ecosystem development in Egypt and the MENA region, she works at the intersection where capital meets impact — helping organizations, DFIs, and mission-driven enterprises translate complex development challenges into measurable outcomes. Her work spans carbon advisory, impact measurement and management, green economy transitions, and investment readiness — supporting accelerators, EU-funded programs, and early-stage companies navigating sustainability compliance and climate finance. Through the 2026 Investor Accelerator, she is building the investor-side lens to complement her operator experience — with a long-term goal of deploying catalytic capital into climate and impact enterprises across Egypt and the MEA region.

name: Yomuma Likessa Daba
bio: Yomuma Likessa is an active venture builder and investment-readiness advisor serving as a strategic bridge for international VCs, DFIs, foundations, and pan-African ESOs looking to deploy capital securely into Ethiopia. Heavily involved in the local ecosystem, he runs and supports Ethiopian-based venture builders. As a key framework contributor to the foundational Startup Ethiopia Proclamation, Yomuma specializes in de-risking market entry, navigating localization, and ensuring regulatory compliance for global allocators. Throughout a decade of ecosystem leadership, he has anchored high-impact enterprise portfolios for DFIs, philanthropic foundations, and VCs. In these roles, he unlocked non-dilutive funding and structured localized diagnostic frameworks to build robust investment-readiness tracks for over 100 high-growth ventures. Yomuma serves as the premier local operating partner for international institutions scaling high-yield venture outcomes.

name: Yousef Shoukry
currentRole: Partnership Manager and Senior Consultant at Takamull AlTanmiah
bio: Yousef is a development practitioner with over eight years of experience advancing economic inclusion, impact investment, and social entrepreneurship across MENA and Africa. He currently serves as Senior Consultant for Global Partnerships & Public Policy at Takamull AlTanmiah. Where he leads cross-border collaborations with multilateral agencies and oversees strategic projects with Saudi public agencies to design policy reforms that strengthen national impact investment ecosystems. Prior to Takamull, Yousef was a Grant Officer and Regional Fellowship Program Associate at Ashoka Arab World, where he managed a network of 120+ Ashoka Fellows, supporting across border collaboration and market expansions. Before that, he designed economic empowerment initiatives at Enroot across six Egyptian governorates — including the "100 Forsa" digital literacy program — in partnership with GIZ, UNIDO, and the ILO. Yousef is currently completing his Master's in Public Policy at the American University in Cairo, with research focused on sustainable finance and Egypt's transition from aid-dependence toward market-impact-driven capital, and previously completed an exchange program at the Geneva Graduate Institute. A long-time Global Shaper with the World Economic Forum and founder of ZShapers and VIA Club. Yousef is passionate about leveraging venture capital to channel patient, mission-aligned capital into African and MENA ecosystems and to scale the next generation of founders solving the continent's most pressing challenges.

name: Zekarias Amsalu
location: Washington DC / Kigali / Addis Ababa, United States / Rwanda / Ethiopia
currentRole: Co-Founder, Africa Fintech Summit & Alpha Expo Micro Accelerator
bio: Zekarias Amsalu (USA/UK/Ethiopia) Linkedin One of the Global Top 100 Most Influential Person of African Descent under 40(MIPAD) for 2018 under Business & Entrepreneurship, Zekarias is Co-Founder & Co-organiser of the premier Africa fintech Summit (https://africafintechsummit.com/) as well as the Founder & MD of Ibex Frontier LLC, Route-to-Africa-market consultancy firm based in Washington DC. For nearly a decade, Zekarias Amsalu — alongside his exceptional team — has co‑hosted biannual Africa Fintech Summit gatherings in Washington, D.C. and across major African cities. Through that work, he built a clear conviction: Africa’s fintech ecosystem deserves a global stage on its own terms. From putting the right narrative of the African fintech ecosystem to carefully selecting and accelerating African early stage startups through his flagship Alpha Expo Micro Accelerator & Pitch Competition Program, Zekarias has helped over 100+ African early stage startups get visibility, access and investor connection over the last 9 years while awarding participating startups over $2 Million worth of awards and benefits, as a resulting helping cohorts go on scale with over $400M in growth capital. A thought-leader & voice and advocate of the African fintech ecosystem, Zekarias has been featured on various international media outlets including Pan African Vision’s cover story “Inside Africa's $65B Fintech Boom with Zekarias Amsalu”, Top Global Voice to follow on Stablecoin, Empower Africa’s top 35 Tech Titans in Africa, Forbes Africa, CNN, CGTN, Digest Africa, Global Finance Magazine, PYMNTS.TV. , Africa Fintech Newsletter, and CGTN, among others. A seasoned speaker and moderator, Zekarias has moderated several high level international events including at the African Union, US-Africa Investment Summit, and at the UNGA side events! Zekarias is a Chartered Certified Accountant (FCCA) and an MBA Graduate of Oxford Brookes University in the UK and lives in Virginia, USA splitting his time with frequent travel to Africa.

name: Afolake Dauda
currentRole: Executive Office Specialist (Strategy)- Drugstoc Ehub Limited
bio: Afolake is a strategy and operations resource with over 7 years of post-grad experience supporting executive leadership across banking, fintech, and healthtech sectors. She currently works at a tech-enabled pharmaceutical distribution company in Nigeria, where she supports strategic initiatives, investor-related processes, and executive decision-making. She is also an MBA candidate at Ajayi Crowther University. Beyond her professional work, she is passionate about volunteer work focused on improving access to food and quality education through the InnerCity Mission for Children. Afolake is thrilled to be part of the Dream VC 2026 cohort and looks forward to deepening her investment judgment while contributing to the growth of Africa’s innovation ecosystem.

name: Aishat Yusuf
currentRole: Venture Analyst at Pennington Promise Capital
bio: Aishat is an Economics graduate and FMVA-certified analyst with over three years of experience across the development and innovation ecosystem in Africa. She is deeply interested in leveraging finance and investment to address development challenges and unlock sustainable economic growth across the continent. Her experience spans climate resilience, gender inclusion, economic development, and startup ecosystem engagement, having contributed to initiatives in partnership with government agencies, development organizations, and ecosystem stakeholders. Aishat currently works as a Venture Analyst, where she supports startup sourcing, investment analysis, ecosystem research, and founder engagement. Through her work, she is building at the intersection of capital, innovation, and impact, with a long-term focus on strengthening Africa’s venture and development landscape.

name: Alice Opiyo
bio: Alice is a manager at a fintech company specializing in marketplace lending through alternative credit. She holds a BS in commerce from the University of Virginia which served as the catalyst for her interest in the intersection of finance and social impact. Her work experience includes financial modeling, project management, treasury, and operations allowing her to hone both quantitative and qualitative skills. Alice currently lives in New York City, but she is excited to move to Nairobi in September to spend more time with her extended family while also being at the forefront of African innovation. When not at work Alice enjoys traveling, hiking, photography, and reading books about niche subjects.

name: Amal Ridene
bio: Amal is a climate adaptation and resilience consultant at Cadlas, advising multilateral institutions on climate finance and investment mobilisation. Prior to her current role, Amal spent four years at AfricInvest — a pan-African private equity firm — where she supported investor relations and fundraising, contributing to the close of AfricInvest Fund IV ($411M) and managing relationships with more than 40 institutional investors including DFIs, sovereign wealth funds, and family offices across Europe, the Middle East, and North America. A Chevening Scholar with an MSc in Sustainable Development from the University of Sussex, she previously served as Tunisia's Climate Finance Negotiator at the UNFCCC across COP26–COP28, working alongside governments, development banks, and private finance actors through the UN High-Level Climate Champions team. Trilingual in Arabic, English, and French, Amal brings deep familiarity with both Francophone and Anglophone African markets. She also brings experience in international governance, having served as a board member of the World Organization of the Scout Movement and currently chairing its Ethics Committee.

name: Andrew Muthotho
bio: Andrew Muthotho is a lawyer and analyst based in Nairobi, Kenya, currently building his practice at IKM Advocates (DLA Piper Africa), where he works across corporate transactions, litigation, and infrastructure matters. He is also a CFA Level 1 candidate, deepening his financial fluency as he works at the intersection of law, business, and capital markets. Andrew is deeply interested in business strategy and what it actually takes for African companies to scale beyond their home markets to genuine global relevance. He believes Africa is the world's defining frontier market, one that is consistently underestimated because it is measured against lagging indicators that fail to capture the pace and nature of its growth. His intellectual interest in African venture capital goes beyond funding mechanics to the structural questions that matter most: how capital vehicles need to be redesigned, how fund timelines must be rethought, and what hybrid instruments could unlock the kind of patient, growth-oriented capital that African businesses need to compete on a global stage. He writes a Substack publication called Into The Workshop, where he publishes strategic analyses of African startups and business models, and has been involved in early-stage investing through angel networks in Nairobi. Beyond his professional pursuits, Andrew is a self-taught visual artist who began painting as a child, stretching canvases with improvised tools and doing odd jobs to buy supplies. That maker instinct has followed him into everything he does. He recently finished second-runners up in Kenya's national virtual stock trading competition, having built his own research pipeline from scratch to get there.

name: Azza Djemel
bio: Azza is an entrepreneurship enabler with over three years of experience in startup support, innovation consulting, and ecosystem building across Africa. Currently a Projects Manager at Flouci (by Kaoun), she has previously worked as an Innovation Consultant at EY Tunisia, focusing on open innovation, and as Programs Assistant at Betawaves, where she designed and delivered incubation and acceleration programs throughout the continent. Her work has supported startups across various stages from investment readiness to scaling while engaging corporates, governments, development agencies, and funds as key stakeholders. A 2025 recipient of the U.S. Embassy's Alumni Engagement Innovation Fund, Azza is implementing an innovation program supporting social startups across four Tunisian cities. A firm believer in the potential of Africa's youth, she joins the Dream VC fellowship eager to deepen her understanding of venture capital and contribute to building a more robust and inclusive African startup ecosystem.

name: Chinenyenwa Udenta
bio: Chinenyenwa is an early-career finance professional with an economics background. She began her career at Parthian Securities, supporting equity research and developing a keen interest in how investment decisions shape business growth and economic outcomes. Since then, she has worked across several multinational organisations, gaining experience in operations, consulting, and financial analysis. Outside of work, Chinenyenwa is actively involved in mentorship and volunteering, supporting initiatives focused on youth and women’s empowerment. She is currently building toward a career in venture capital, with a focus on backing businesses that drive sustainable development and long-term value creation across Africa.

name: Chioma Agu
bio: Chioma Agu is a product manager passionate about building technology that expands access and improves everyday experiences. Over the past two years, she has worked within fintech, contributing to savings, investment, and lending products while collaborating across product, engineering, operations, and business teams to drive user-focused solutions. Originally trained in Cell Biology and Genetics, Chioma transitioned into technology driven by a curiosity for systems, human behavior, and solving meaningful problems at scale. Beyond product delivery, she is deeply interested in startup ecosystems, innovation, and how capital and strategic support can help early-stage companies grow across Africa. She is passionate about learning, community-building, and supporting initiatives that create opportunities for the next generation of African builders and innovators.

name: Cuan Solomon
bio: Cuan Solomon is a Senior Consulting Associate at with over seven years of expertise spanning banking, impact investing, green finance, and the blue economy. He specializes in designing and executing climate-focused accelerators and pitching challenges, providing critical technical assistance to help green economy startups unlock capital and achieve investment readiness. Armed with a background in development finance, Cuan is dedicated to scaling entrepreneurship support pathways across Africa.

name: Danladi Momodu
bio: Danladi is a management consultant with experience advising clients across financial services, technology, and energy on corporate strategy, business transformation, and international expansion. Prior to consulting, he held commercial roles at a Fortune 500 pharmaceutical company and a healthtech startup, experiences that shaped his interest in how innovation and capital allocation decisions influence economic outcomes in emerging markets. He holds a Doctor of Pharmacy (Pharm.D) degree from University of Benin. He co-founded the Benin-City Hub of the Global Shapers Community, an initiative of the World Economic Forum, where he led strategic initiatives across sustainability, the future of work, and community development. Outside of work, Danladi enjoys swimming and exploring ideas around economic development and Africa’s evolving business landscape.

name: David Norman Masoperh
bio: David Masoperh is the Co-founder of Pebla, an offline-first fintech super app building financial infrastructure for underserved African markets. Based in Kigali, David operates at the intersection of fintech, product, and ecosystem building, with a focus on solving real-world solutions in low-connectivity environments. David holds a background in engineering and product management, with experience spanning fintech, AI-enabled systems, and early-stage venture building. He holds a Master of Science in Information Technology from Carnegie Mellon University, where he deepened his focus on technology-driven solutions for emerging markets and developed a strong interest in financial infrastructure, startup ecosystems, and venture-scale innovation across Africa. David is deeply interested in the future of African financial systems & embedded finance. He is particularly passionate about building infrastructure that serves the realities of African consumers. Outside of work, he enjoys dance and writing about technology, markets, and the future of Africa’s digital economy.

name: DayeAbasi David
currentRole: Legal Counsel at Ceed Venture Studio
bio: DayeAbasi David is a startup and venture lawyer, passionate about the growth of Africa’s innovation and venture capital landscape. Her work focuses on the intersection of law, startups, technology, venture financing, and storytelling, She currently contributes to the African startup ecosystem through her work with Ceed Venture Studios, Founders Friday - Uyo, and Founders Stories With Daye (FSWD), https://substack.com/@didi04 where she supports founder communities, ecosystem engagement, and conversations around entrepreneurship, innovation, and the founders journey. As a storyteller, her focus is on amplifying founder journeys and shaping narratives that highlight the realities and opportunities within Africa’s tech ecosystem. DayeAbasi is particularly interested in venture capital, startup growth, and ecosystem development, and is committed to supporting ambitious founders access capital, while building a more globally competitive and founder-friendly African innovation ecosystem.

name: Diana Kamau
currentRole: Operations and Community Manager, The Engine
bio: Diana Kamau is Kenyan - American.
